subject.title: Add Tailscale Serve support for WSL gateways

question: After the least-privilege and route-validation fixes, should generated gateways enable gateway.auth.allowTailscale and treat tailnet identity plus ACLs as a supported core authentication boundary?
rationale: The two patch defects have mechanical repairs, but accepting a new identity trust model and its long-term support expectations requires repository owner intent.

options.title: Approve opt-in identity trust
options.body: Accept allowTailscale with clear setup disclosure, preserved token/device flows, and focused security and failure-path proof.

options.title: Use private transport only
options.body: Provision Tailscale Serve for connectivity but continue requiring OpenClaw token or device authentication for every connection.

options.title: Defer core integration
options.body: Pause the feature until the authentication policy and long-term Tailscale support ownership are established.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in identity trust
recommendation.body: Accept allowTailscale with clear setup disclosure, preserved token/device flows, and focused security and failure-path proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the generated Windows gateway onboarding architecture and is the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether this new core setup and authentication mode belongs in that product path.
